constants.value: An unofficial engine for Zero Tolerance (Sega Mega Drive / Genesis, 1994). It needs your own ROM image and is not affiliated with Sega, Technopop or Accolade.
Using the original ROM image, made royalty-free for distribution by its copyright owner (technopop.net). Cancel to pick your own.

value: The same world at your screen's resolution: widescreen, sharp textures, smooth motion. The original picture is one switch away.
Turn with the mouse; jump, crouch, fire and pick weapons with their own keys. Or keep the controller's combinations.
Play the whole game with a friend online: one opens a room, the other joins with its code.
Ten switches for the game's own cheat codes, on or off at any time from the menu.
Start any level from its password; the passwords you reach are kept for you.
Save the game at any moment and load it back, a key each.

data.order: character index 0..4 as in the character-select screen

row.end: a zero item id ends the row
row.pair: item id word, then amount word; the high byte of the amount is the count

data.vector_ids: logical ids from the harness vocabulary; the same ids label the entity slots in world snapshots (checked against the world schema's id lists, except the link-mode ids)

data.fire_dispatch: items and fire routines share one id space: the fire table is indexed by item id (documented; the passive items dispatching exactly like id 0 is what proves it)

kinds.passive: dispatches to the same fire routine as no item at all (unarmed)
kinds.tool: has its own fire routine but is not a weapon (documentation)
kinds.weapon: has its own fire routine (documentation: it damages or places something)

other_pickups.effect: adds to the player's health word unless it is already 100 (then the tile stays)

pickup_rule.class_to_item: classes 25..36 give item id (class - 24); class 130 gives item 13 and class 54 gives item 14; class 37 is the medipack; class 38 has no effect (its trigger is empty)
pickup_rule.trigger: the map-tile trigger table sends exactly the classes listed in items and other_pickups to the pickup handler

consumer_shapes.expression: signed(state) >> 4, then the low byte or the low 9 bits of each 16-bit half

data.draw_order: one global stream: the number and the order of draws before a consumer are part of its outcome

low_bits.consequence: a test of the low bits is locked to the number of draws since the seed
low_bits.cycle_length_rule: the low m bits cycle with length 2^(m-1) for m >= 2 and 2 for m = 1

hardware_recipe.term: each read is taken as a signed 16-bit value and added to the 32-bit sum
hardware_recipe.when: each time the game runs its seeding routine; the ROM calls it from three places

seeding.policy: explicit scenario parameter: every scenario states the seed the generator starts from

data.wrap: the product wraps at 32 bits; it exceeds 2^53, so a double-precision product is wrong

key.rule: byte n = low byte of k; then k = rotate-right-32(k, 7), then swap the two 16-bit halves

end_of_table.rule: the table ends at the first 3-byte group whose first byte is not a mode 0..3; that group is the start of a code routine, called from elsewhere in the ROM

data.ids_beyond_table: ids >= entry_count read code bytes; they are not part of this table

data.entry_layout: per angle: sin256 then neg_cos256, two signed 16-bit words, big-endian in the ROM
